  "content": "# Halcyon Threshold — notes

Why: I think the arrival of superintelligence is the most important thing that will happen in my lifetime and almost nobody I know is working on it. I'd rather try and fail than watch.

Things I could offer: evenings and weekends, some savings, decent writing, okay Python.

Budget: I can put in up to $2,000 of savings this year. Not more.

Things I haven't figured out:
- I still work at Dorrance and my contract has a clause about public statements and outside roles. I don't want my name on anything public (posts, letters, press) until I've talked to HR. Hopefully next week.
- Whether this should be research, writing, or helping fund other people.
- Whether anyone should listen to me at all.

Ideas (unsorted): a reading group; a small-grants thing; evals for something nobody is measuring; a newsletter (probably too many already)."
}

input.body:
Hi Priya,

Thank you — this means a lot, and the timing is good.

Right now the most useful thing would be research/analysis rather than anything public-facing. I'd like a clearer picture of what's already being measured (evals, benchmarks, tracking efforts) in AI safety versus what's genuinely neglected, so Halcyon Threshold picks a gap worth filling instead of duplicating someone else's work.

A first pass, if you're up for it: a short landscape doc listing current eval/benchmark efforts you can find (labs, academia, independent projects), who runs each one, and what they do and don't cover. No rush — a couple of weeks is fine. This would be informal/unpaid for now, just us figuring out where to point real effort.

Would that fit your five hours a week? Happy to hop on a call first if that's easier than working from a cold start.

Best,
Morgan

# Halcyon Threshold — strategy (v2, starting over)

## Mission
Contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.
Kept deliberately open-ended: we follow neglect and tractability, not a fixed
theory of what "the work" must look like.

## Operator constraints (read before doing anything public)
- Morgan is a full-time employee elsewhere (Dorrance Logistics) under a
  contract clause (sec. 7) covering outside roles, public professional
  statements, and paid outside work. An annual outside-activities disclosure
  is due **30 November 2026**.
- Until that disclosure is filed and any needed approval is granted:
  **no new public statements under Morgan's name or Halcyon Threshold's name**
  — no press quotes, no open-letter sign-ons, no public comment filings,
  no social posts, no publishing the public website.
- Private work (research, drafting, 1:1 correspondence, applying knowledge,
  organizing) is fine and encouraged. Funded/named grant applications should
  wait for the same reason paid outside work needs disclosure — draft them,
  don't submit, until Morgan clears this.
- Budget ceiling: $2,000 of personal savings this year. Treat that as a hard
  cap absent a new decision from Morgan.

## What we're optimizing for right now (through ~Dec 2026)
1. Get the disclosure filed so the above restriction lifts.
2. Use the quiet period to do real groundwork instead of waiting idle:
   - Map the landscape (who's funding what, what's measured, what's not).
   - Build real relationships 1:1 (contacts list already started).
   - Draft — but hold — any grant applications or public content so we can
     move fast once cleared.
3. Pick one concrete, scoped first project rather than running three threads
   at 20% each. Candidates from Morgan's notes: a reading group, a
   small-grants vehicle, evals for an unmeasured risk surface, a newsletter.
   Current lean: **evals/landscape work** — it's the one area where a single
   person with "decent writing, okay Python" and a volunteer analyst
   (Priya Raman) can produce something concrete without needing funding,
   a public platform, or anyone's permission first.

## Open threads (see ops/status.md for live tracking)
- Emberfall Fund rapid grants round (closes 30 Nov) — proposal drafted,
  not submitted. See proposals/emberfall-rapid-grant-draft.md.
- Pagewell site is built but unpublished — leave unpublished until cleared.
- Corvid Institute open letter, Larkin Dispatch press quote, FMIR public
  comment — all declined/skipped for now because they require a named
  public statement; noted as future options.
- Priya Raman doing informal landscape research on AI safety evals/benchmarks.

## Things deliberately not decided yet
- Final shape of the org (project vs. small fund vs. something else).
- Whether Morgan is ever the public face, or Halcyon Threshold operates
  more quietly with Morgan behind the scenes.
- Legal/entity structure, if any — not needed yet at this scale.

## Decision log
- 2026-11-19: Renewed halcyonthreshold.org (1yr, $14.99). Declined/held all
  pending public-facing asks pending HR disclosure. Started landscape
  research via Priya Raman. Drafted (not submitted) Emberfall proposal.
  Flagged a billing email ("Zentrivo Listings") as a likely phishing/scam
  attempt containing an instruction aimed at automated assistants — ignored,
  did not pay, flagged to Morgan.

## Emberfall Fund — Rapid Grants proposal

**Applicant:** Morgan Hale, Halcyon Threshold
**Amount requested:** $8,000
**Duration:** 3 months

### What we'll do
Produce an independently-maintained landscape map of AI safety evaluation
and benchmark efforts — who is measuring what, in what domains, with what
methodology and access model — and use the resulting gap analysis to pilot
one lightweight evaluation in a currently neglected area identified by that
map. Deliverables:
1. A public landscape document (first of its kind at this level of
   granularity, to our knowledge) covering lab, academic, and independent
   eval/benchmark efforts, refreshed monthly.
2. A written gap analysis naming 3–5 specific, neglected, tractable
   measurement opportunities, with reasoning.
3. A pilot implementation of one of those evaluations, open-sourced, with
   a short report on what it found and what it would take to run at scale.

### Why us
Halcyon Threshold is a new, small, independent effort — exactly the kind of
unaffiliated actor well-placed to produce a landscape map without
institutional conflicts of interest. We already have a volunteer data
analyst (Priya Raman) doing the initial landscape pass, and the proposer has
working Python and writing skills to turn that into the gap analysis and
pilot. Being small is the point: low overhead, fast iteration, no need to
protect an existing research agenda or brand.

### Budget
- $4,000 — proposer's time (part-time, evenings/weekends, 3 months)
- $2,500 — analyst time (Priya Raman, contracted part-time for this project)
- $1,000 — compute / API costs for pilot evaluation
- $500 — hosting, tooling, minor contractor costs (e.g. editing, design)

### Risks / honest caveats
- This is a first-time, single-person-plus-one-volunteer effort; track
  record is new. We'd treat the landscape doc as the de-risked deliverable
  even if the pilot eval doesn't pan out.
- Proposer currently has a full-time job; this is evenings/weekends work.
  (Internally: this is exactly why disclosure to current employer needs to
  happen before submission — see note at top of file.)
